content.comment_body: Hello everyone. Is it possible to use the ESC and OK keys on the [product_name] via its Web Server, similar to how they are used directly on the module for menu settings? Any advice appreciated. Thanks for the help, [user_name]

Within the program, only the cursor keys on the basic module can be processed. For [product_name], both cursor keys and the four F-keys are utilized. The program recognizes cursor keys only if the ESC key is held down while pressing a cursor key.
Hi, that's correct. From my past experience, I used the cursor keys for adjusting operator settings, which worked only when used together with ESC, OK, or one of the F-keys.
So, does that mean the ESC and OK keys have no effect through the Web Server?
On the Web Server, the ESC and OK keys behave the same way as they do on the actual [product_name] or [product_name] device.

To clarify further, I created a demonstration video. For the cursor keys to work in the program, you must first press the ESC key, which changes the colors of the left/right cursor keys. The program also includes a message that needs to be confirmed. This message stays active until you press the OK key. As shown, both the ESC and OK buttons indeed have a function.
Thank you so much! That's clear now. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The original user was uncertain about whether ESC and OK keys on the [product_name] could be used via the Web Server. Other participants clarified these keys function similarly to how they do on the physical device or compatible panels, performing roles like activating cursor key actions or confirming messages within the program. The initial confusion stemmed from limited documentation or unclear correspondence between hardware controls and their virtual counterparts.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes that the ESC and OK keys will work through the Web Server interface and offer the same capabilities found on the physical module.
